newsitem.title: USA: Digital sees Alpha sales turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Digital sees Alpha sales turnaround.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp Chief Financial Officer Vincent Mullarkey said Thursday revenues from sales of computer systems based on its Alpha microprocessors fell year-over-year in the fourth quarter.
But he said those revenues should grow on a year-over-year basis beginning in the first quarter.
"Quarter four Alpha revenues showed an improvement of 15 percent versus quarter three, and a decline of four percent, year-over-year," he told reporters on a conference call.
When asked about when he expected a year-over-year turnaround, he said in the current first quarter.
Mullarkey said Alpha servers had year-over-year growth in the mid-single digits, but sales of Alpha workstations have declined, accounting for the drop in total Alpha sales.

Overall revenues also fell year-over-year in the fourth quarter, but he said those should also turn around in the first quarter. "We expect, as we move into fiscal year 1998, to begin reporting revenue growth, and I hope that begins as soon as this (first) quarter," he said.
Currency fluctuations hit Digital's earnings to the tune of $80 million in the fourth quarter, and $240 million over the full year, Mullarkey said.
"We're quite optimistic about our profit prospects in the next year," Mullarkey added.
He said most of the decline in year-over-year revenues was due to businesses that Digital had exited over the course of the year and the currency fluctuations.
Mullarkey said he expected the bulk of the authorized repurchase of 15 million of Digital's own shares will be bought over the next 12 months.
"I generally expect the lion's share will be purchased over the next 12 months or so," he said.
Digital closed the 1997 fiscal year with 151.1 million shares outstanding, he said.

Chief Executive Robert Palmer said on the conference call that Digital expected to "maintain a reasonable commercial relationship" with Intel Corp despite its patent infringement lawsuit against the chip maker.

"They have scheduled orders for delivery for the fourth quarter through this calendar year and we expect to receive the information we need necessary to design their products into our systems," he said.
"We remain convinced that we will be able to provide competitive systems to our customers based on the Intel architecture, and we have plans to do that," he added.
